title: Erasing History or Removing Propaganda? DOJ Deletes Jan 6 Case Files From Website
subtitle: The Department of Justice removed hundreds of press releases related to January 6 prosecutions from its website, calling them 'partisan propaganda' from the Biden administration.

conservative.headline: Justice Department Strips Biden-Era Partisan Propaganda From Official Website
conservative.byline: As seen on Fox News, The Hill, CNBC
paragraphs: The Department of Justice is finally cleaning house, removing what officials describe as blatantly partisan propaganda left over from the Biden administration's politically motivated prosecution of January 6 defendants.

When confronted about the deletions, the DOJ didn't apologize—they doubled down. The department's official Rapid Response account declared they are proud to reverse the DOJ's weaponization under the Biden administration and committed to stripping the website of partisan propaganda used to persecute Americans for political purposes.

This move follows President Trump's mass pardons of over 1,500 January 6 defendants, correcting what he has repeatedly called one of the greatest injustices in American history. These were citizens who were subjected to excessive prosecutions, pre-dawn raids, and years-long legal harassment simply because they supported the wrong political candidate.

The Biden DOJ turned the Justice Department into a weapon against conservatives, using inflammatory press releases to paint peaceful protesters as insurrectionists and seditionists. By removing these biased documents, the current administration is restoring integrity to an institution that was thoroughly corrupted under the previous regime.

Not every Republican agrees with every aspect of the Trump DOJ's approach. Senator Thom Tillis called the department's new compensation fund a payout pot for punks, and Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell dismissed it as a slush fund to pay people who assault cops. But even these critics don't dispute the fundamental problem: the Biden administration used the Justice Department as a political weapon.

The deleted press releases weren't neutral legal updates—they were carefully crafted propaganda pieces designed to shape public opinion against Trump supporters. They served no legitimate legal purpose after cases were resolved, but remained on the website as monuments to partisan persecution.

Democrats are predictably outraged, not because they care about government transparency, but because they're losing control of the narrative. For four years, they used these inflammatory press releases to justify their witch hunt against ordinary Americans who dared to question the 2020 election.
The Trump DOJ isn't hiding anything—it's correcting the historical record and ending the weaponization of federal law enforcement. That's not erasing history; it's finally telling the truth.

liberal.headline: Trump DOJ Scrubs Public Records of Jan 6 Criminal Cases, Critics Warn
liberal.byline: As seen on MSNBC, NBC News, House Judiciary Democrats
paragraphs: In an Orwellian attempt to rewrite history, the Trump Justice Department has systematically deleted hundreds of press releases documenting the criminal prosecutions of January 6 rioters who violently attacked the U.S. Capitol in an attempt to overturn a democratic election.

When questioned about quietly scrubbing public records, the DOJ didn't even pretend to care about transparency. Instead, officials proudly announced they were reversing the DOJ's weaponization and stripping the website of what they called partisan propaganda—which is to say, accurate descriptions of seditious conspiracy, assault on law enforcement, and violent attacks on our democracy.

Senate Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Dick Durbin warned that the notion of compensating January 6 rioters is absurd and offensive, particularly for those who violently assaulted Capitol Police and Metropolitan Police officers trying to defend our seat of government.

Representative Jamie Raskin didn't mince words, calling the DOJ's $1.776 billion compensation fund pure fraud and highway robbery. In testimony before the House Judiciary Committee, Raskin said that with election deniers Pam Bondi and Kash Patel running the Justice Department, it's like the Joker and the Riddler and the Penguin have taken over Gotham City.

Representative Joe Neguse captured the brazenness of this corruption, noting that taxpayer money will be used to compensate the very people who attacked our Capitol. He called it unconscionable. It is corrupt. and demanded accountability from Republican leadership who remain silent.

This isn't about removing outdated information—it's about erasing evidence of one of the darkest days in American history. The deleted press releases documented seditious conspiracy convictions against Proud Boys and Oath Keepers leaders, detailed assaults on law enforcement officers, and chronicled the breadth of the criminal conspiracy to overturn the 2020 election.

The timing is no coincidence. After Trump pardoned more than 1,500 January 6 defendants—including those convicted of violently attacking police officers—his Justice Department is now systematically removing the evidence of their crimes from the public record. It's the digital equivalent of burning books.

This is textbook authoritarianism: rewrite history, reward political violence, and punish those who tell the truth. Every American should be alarmed when the Justice Department becomes a propaganda ministry for the president who incited the attack in the first place.

The Trump administration isn't correcting the record—it's erasing it. And in doing so, they're ensuring that future generations won't fully understand how close America came to losing its democracy on January 6, 2021.

factcheck.headline: Separating Fact from Spin
paragraphs: Both sides are presenting selective versions of the same event to serve their political narratives. Here's what actually happened and what it means.
THE UNDISPUTED FACTS:

✓ The deletions are real: The Department of Justice removed hundreds of press releases related to January 6 prosecutions from its official website in late May 2026, as confirmed by multiple news outlets after Washington Post reporter Meryl Kornfield noticed the missing documents.

✓ DOJ acknowledged it openly: The department's Rapid Response account publicly stated they were removing what they characterized as partisan propaganda from the Biden era and making whole those they claim were politically persecuted.

✓ This follows mass pardons: President Trump pardoned more than 1,500 January 6 defendants in January 2025, including individuals convicted of assaulting law enforcement officers and seditious conspiracy.

✓ A compensation fund exists: The DOJ announced a $1.776 billion fund on May 20, 2026, and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has not ruled out payments to January 6 defendants, as reported by NBC News.

✓ Bipartisan criticism exists: Republican Senators Thom Tillis and Mitch McConnell both criticized the compensation fund, with Tillis calling it politically tone-deaf and McConnell dismissing it as a slush fund.
CONSERVATIVE SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: These were peaceful protesters persecuted for political beliefs. Reality: Federal courts—including judges appointed by Republicans—convicted defendants based on extensive evidence of violence, conspiracy, and assaults on law enforcement. More than 140 officers were injured. The prosecutions were based on criminal conduct, not political viewpoint.

⚠️ Claim: The press releases were pure propaganda with no legal purpose. Reality: DOJ press releases serve legitimate purposes including public accountability, deterrence, and transparency about how justice is administered. They're standard practice across all administrations for major cases.
✓ Fair point: Some Biden administration rhetoric about January 6 was politically charged, and reasonable people can debate whether every prosecution was proportionate to the offense committed.
LIBERAL SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: This is unprecedented authoritarian censorship. Reality: While highly unusual and politically motivated, the actual case files, court records, and legal documents remain publicly available through the federal court system. The press releases were summaries, not the underlying evidence.

⚠️ Claim: All January 6 defendants were violent insurrectionists. Reality: The cases ranged widely—from people who committed serious assaults and seditious conspiracy to those who simply entered the building and left. Not all cases involved violence, though the event itself was undeniably violent.
✓ Fair point: Removing accurate government records to support a political narrative about pardoned defendants is troubling and undermines public trust in the Justice Department's independence.
THE BIGGER PICTURE:

This controversy reflects a fundamental disagreement about January 6 itself. Conservatives increasingly view it as a protest that got out of hand, exploited by Democrats for political gain. Liberals see it as a violent attempt to overturn democracy that must be remembered and never minimized.

Both sides miss important nuance: It's possible to believe that January 6 was a serious attack on democratic processes AND that some prosecutions may have been excessive. It's possible to support accountability for violence AND question whether a compensation fund for pardoned defendants serves justice.

The real damage here isn't just about deleted press releases—it's about the Justice Department being repeatedly used as a political weapon by both parties, eroding public confidence in equal justice under law.

The Bottom Line: The DOJ removed accurate public records for political reasons, following presidential pardons that themselves were politically motivated. Whether you call it correcting injustice or erasing history depends entirely on what you believe about January 6—and neither partisan narrative captures the full complexity of what happened that day or how justice was administered afterward.
